references.title: Flammability, Offgassing, and Compatibility Requirements and Test Procedures

items.text: Test 1 determines whether a material, when exposed to a standard ignition source, will self-extinguish and not transfer burning debris that can ignite adjacent materials.
items.quote: The purpose of this test is to determine if a material, when exposed to a standard ignition source, will self-extinguish and not transfer burning debris, which can ignite adjacent materials.

items.text: Test 1 evaluates the material in the worst-case atmosphere to which it could be exposed; the oxygen level is the highest the material could witness in use.
Five specimens of 30 cm by 6.5 cm, mounted vertically and ignited at the bottom.
A material is self-extinguishing if no specimen burns more than 15 cm and no specimen propagates a flame by transfer of burning debris.
Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC): the maximum oxygen concentration at which at least five specimens pass the acceptance criteria of Test 1.
items.quote: Maximum Oxygen Concentration: The maximum oxygen concentration at which at least five specimens pass the acceptance criteria of this test.

items.text: Air shall not be allowed to flow during tests.
items.quote: Air shall not be allowed to flow during tests.

items.text: Ambient conditions: 20.9 percent oxygen, 101.4 kPa (14.7 psia), 23 +/-5 degC.

items.text: The vehicle shall have a fire protection system composed of detecting, warning, and extinguishing devices that do not create a hazardous environment.
items.quote: The vehicle shall have a fire protection system composed of detecting, warning, and extinguishing devices that do not create a hazardous environment to all spacecraft volumes during all mission phases.

items.text: A fire protection system shall include manually operated portable fire extinguishers.
The system shall monitor in real time the toxic combustion products of Table 6.2-3 and alert the crew.

Recommended combustion product monitoring ranges: CO 5-1000 ppm (accuracy +/-10%, resolution 1 ppm); HCN 2-50 ppm; HCl 2-50 ppm; HF 2-50 ppm, or total halide acid gases HX 2-50 ppm (+/-25%, 1 ppm). ppm by volume at 1 atm.

items.text: Fire safety capability areas: (1) fire prevention and material flammability, (2) fire detection, (3) fire suppression, (4) post-fire clean-up.
items.quote: Fire safety is divided into capability areas that include: (1) fire prevention and material flammability, (2) fire detection, (3) fire suppression, and (4) post-fire clean-up.

items.text: Prevention means eliminating one of the three fire-causing factors: fuel, oxygen, ignition energy.
ISS response: after detection, ventilation in the affected module is terminated to slow the spread of fire; a portable CO2 extinguisher is used in the U.S. modules.
items.where: ISS Fire Safety Strategy, steps 2 and 5

items.text: Design requirements need to specify the pressure and percent O2 combinations permitted in the habitable volume.

items.text: Detectors respond to fire signatures: temperature rise, combustion gases, light and other radiation, particulates (smoke), pressure rise, acoustic waves. Rapid detection with limited false alarms is required.

The rate of buildup of atmospheric gases, particularly carbon monoxide, is an additional early warning; after a fire the module stays isolated until CO, HCN and HCl are reduced to admissible concentrations.
items.where: Overview; ISS Fire Safety Strategy step 8

items.text: The extinguishing agent must not support combustion in an O2-enriched environment, contain toxic agents, emit toxic products, interfere with visual observation, or be slow to initiate.
Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap; exploration brings increased oxygen content in a low-pressure atmosphere and intermediate gravity levels.
items.quote: Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap for exploration missions.

items.text: Carbon monoxide SMAC: 1 hour 425 ppm, 24 hour 100 ppm, 7 day 55 ppm, 30 day 15 ppm, 180 day 15 ppm, 1000 day 15 ppm. Effects: CNS depression, cardiac arrhythmia.

SMACs are set for and applicable to ambient conditions (14.7 psi, 25 degC) and to spacecraft cabin air; 1- and 24-hour values apply to off-nominal situations. They are crew exposure guidelines, not limits for a test chamber.
Pressures listed for unit conversion: 14.7 psia, and 10.2 and 8.2 psia as proposed atmospheres for upcoming missions.

The recommendations require materials ignition and flammability testing and certification up to 34% oxygen, and a modified standard flammability test to generate ignition threshold data.

items.text: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI): the oxygen mole fraction below which a steady flame cannot exist for a given material and ambient condition. In total flooding, the goal of the agent is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI.

items.text: Minimum Extinction Concentration (MEC): the minimum suppressant concentration above which a quasi-steady flame cannot exist. LOI = 0.209 (1 - MEC).
